document.title: Afghan-Pak Border Relations at Torkham Tense (Peshaw 00916)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Confidential] A consulate contact witnessed 30-35 sealed ISI trucks and 15-20 fuel tankers waiting to cross at Torkham and was certain of the convoy's ISI affiliation. The cable does not specify the contents or destination.

events.description: Pakistani authorities closed the border at Torkham for about four days, possibly bracing for a Kabul refugee influx.
Afghans threw stones at the Pakistan Border Guard, who fired into the air; the border reopened around 2000 hrs, letting the 'ISI convoy' and pedestrians cross.
Colonel Hafiz told a U.S. officer that the border had been closed four days and at least 60 families were waiting to repatriate.
The U.S. Consulate Peshawar cable on tensions at Torkham was sent to Washington and other posts.
Torkham border closed for about four days, per Hafiz, with at least 60 families waiting to repatriate and about 2,000 people waiting on each side.
Afghans threw stones at Pakistan Border Guard members at Torkham; guards fired weapons into the air; press reported injuries and one refugee death.
Border reopened at about 2000 hrs, allowing the 'ISI convoy' and pedestrians to cross.
Pakistani officials claimed sixteen Panjshiris were arrested while trying to cross at Torkham.
U.S. Consulate Peshawar cable reporting tension at Torkham, calling the 250,000 Kabul departure estimates overstated.

key_claims: An apparent ISI convoy of 30-35 sealed trucks and 15-20 fuel tankers was waiting to cross into Afghanistan at Torkham on 30 Sep 1996, shortly after the Taliban took Kabul.
The source identified the convoy as ISI from the licence plates and from tea with its officers in charge.
Reports of 250,000 people leaving Kabul appear greatly overstated.
Pakistan may have closed the border at Torkham to prepare for a Kabul refugee influx that did not materialize.
Pakistani officials claimed that sixteen Panjshiris had been arrested while trying to cross at Torkham.
